meta.question: Can I have the fees waived?

question: Can I have the fees waived?

answers:
If you wish to request a waiver for the $390 filing fee in the Court of Appeal, you must submit a Request to Waive Court Fees form (FW-001) along with your first filing in the Court of Appeal. Submitting this fee waiver form with your initial filing means you will only have to pay fees once the court decides on your fee waiver application. 
You can fill out the Request to Waive Court Fees form (FW-001) online. 
During an appeal, fees are associated with both the trial court and the Court of Appeal. If you are the appellant and wish to have your court fees waived, you must secure a fee waiver from both courts. 
To have fees waived in both courts, you need to complete two fee waiver forms (FW-001)—one for the trial court and one for the Court of Appeal. You should submit both forms to the trial court when you file your notice of appeal. If you already have a fee waiver from the trial court, it may still be valid when you file your notice of appeal. 
Fee waivers expire 60 days after the trial court's judgment. You may qualify for a fee waiver if your household income (before taxes) is less than the amounts specified in item 5b of form FW-001 and if the court determines that you do not have sufficient income to cover basic household needs and court fees.

history.content: How much is the fee to get a copy of the oral argument recording from the court?
I do not have that information.
Can anyone pay a fee to get a copy of an oral argument recording from the court?
Yes. Any party may pay a fee to get a copy of their oral argument recording from the court.
When you say "any party," it refers to the individuals involved in the case, not the general public, correct?
Yes, that's correct. In the courts, the individuals or entities directly involved in the case are referred to as parties; for example, ask for the name of party.

To be eligible for an oral argument, a party must have filed a brief that has been accepted by the Court of Appeal. If the respondent did not file a brief, they cannot make an oral argument. If a party is represented by a lawyer, the lawyer will present the oral argument. A party is not required to attend court for the oral argument if they have legal representation. The court will provide all parties with at least 20 days' advance notice, which will include the date, time, and location of the oral argument.
Can I decline to participate in an oral argument?

Yes. You have the option to decline to participate in an oral argument. If you decide not to make an oral argument, it will not affect the court's view of your arguments in the appeal. Not all parties are required to participate in the same way; if only one party wishes to present an oral argument, the court will hold the oral argument for the case but will not compel the other parties to participate. 
Many appeals do not include oral arguments because all parties choose to waive (give up) their right to do so. When there is no oral argument, the Court of Appeal justices decide based solely on the written briefs and the appeal record. It is important to note that oral arguments do not speed up or delay the appeal process.

evidence.text:
If your request is approved, the courts will generally waive most but not all fees.
Note: If you already have a fee waiver from the trial court, it could still be valid when you file your notice of appeal. Fee waivers expire 60 days after the trial court’s judgment. Please check with your trial court and ask if you need to submit a new fee waiver application.
Learn more about how to qualify and what fees can be waived
Read the California Court’s information sheet on fee waivers
Get a blank fee waiver form FW-001
Get instructions for how to fill out the fee waiver form FW-001
 
 What happens if I don’t pay the notice of appeal filing fees? If you do not pay the filing fees or if your check bounces, the Court of Appeal will send a notice that you have 15 days to pay the fees or have them waived.
If you apply for a fee waiver but the Court of Appeal denies the request, the court will send a notice that you have 15 days to pay the filing fees.

For respondent’s appeal fees in the Court of Appeal:

If you want to request that the Court of Appeal waive your $390 filing fee, you must file a Request to Waive Court Fees form FW-001 in the Court of Appeal.
You will give the Court of Appeal a fee waiver form when you file your first document in the court.

Respondent’s Brief – California Appellate Courts
If you want to request that the Court of Appeal waive your $390 filing fee, you must file a Request to Waive Court Fees form FW-001 with your first filing in the Court of Appeal. If you file a fee waiver form with your first filing, you will not have to pay any fees until the court makes a decision about your fee waiver application.
The Request to Waive Court Fees form FW-001 is available at the court or online.
Note: Form FW-001 is not served to other parties. It is only filed with the court.
Learn more about fee waivers
